notes:
- The received half of the inbox reads its own type now: Messages you were sent can only be listed through AniList's notifications, and that field answers a union - a set of possible row types - which the server can only resolve when the query names the type it wants.
- A frame rate you can set, and what this screen says about itself: How often the sky moves is now its own choice, separate from how much it draws: Auto, 30, 60, 120 or 144 Hz.
- Device management: this phone's numbers, and how much disk the art may take: The Seasonal page now opens with what the device reports - the rate the screen runs at and the rates it can be set to - and adds a cover-cache ceiling you can choose: 256 MB, which is what the app has always kept, up to 5 GB.
- The snow stays off the navigation bar: A winter sky used to leave a cap along the bar's own pill, with drips over its face and a sparkle.
- Hide a message, and see the ones you have not read: Each row in Messages can be dismissed from your list, and a switch on the same row decides whether new arrivals are marked at all.
- Sharp covers, smaller bytes where a slot cannot show more: Posters, backdrops and the full-screen viewer still ask AniList for its largest file - those are the pictures you look at.
- Less work in a frame while you scroll: The animated progress wave rebuilt a fresh path of 96 segments per frame per card - the way a smooth fling turns into a garbage-collection pause when a screenful of cards is on screen - and reuses one path now.
- Ten shapes, ten pictures on the chips: Each Seasonal shape chip draws the sky's own ink, and now poses it: a radius fitted to that shape, the variant that names it at eighteen dots, a small tilt, and a hairline floor so the veins and filaments survive a low-density screen instead of fading to a smudge.
- One hundred and sixty-three more lines, thirty-eight of them dark: The joke pool grows from 1061 to 1224.
- The "Sequel to ..." line now opens the title it names: Every card on the dashboard is about the sequel, and the line above it names the entry the gap is measured against - which was text, and nothing more.
- The artwork behind the cover is now a picture you can tap: In a title's page the banner or key visual fills the top of the sheet, and only the small poster answered a tap: the rest of the image did nothing, while this app's own comment described the full picture as one tap away.
- A GIF index that needs a key says that it never got one: Choosing Klipy, GIPHY or Tenor without a saved key kept working - the anonymous booru answers anime tags for nothing, and that fallback is deliberate - but it happened in silence, so the reader picked one index and received another one's catalogue with nothing connecting the two.
- A sixth GIF index, and it asks for no account: Konachan's safe board joins Safebooru and nekos.best as an index you can search without a key or a signup.
- nekos.best blames itself rather than the network: Searching it for a word that is not one of its reaction names used to send a request the API cannot honour: its search needs a category in its type argument, and a word it has no category for has no valid request at all.
